title: A whole recall never returns an episode longer than its cap on its own
body:
## Summary
`_whole_episodes` admits a first episode longer than the cap only when `spent == 0`, and `recall_whole` always passes the rendered keyword block's cost (at least 30 chars), so that branch never runs: one long matching episode comes back as `(showing 0 of 1)`.

## Description
src/athena/core/recall.py:428 (`if not items and spent == 0 and cost + overhead > cap`) is the only path that leaves an oversized episode to the gate's cut. Its one caller, src/athena/core/recall.py:343-346, passes `_packed_chars(keyword)` plus the reserved note, and the keyword block always renders at least `(showing 0 of 0)`, so `spent` is never 0. The recall_whole docstring ("The one episode ever left to the gate's cut is one longer than the cap on its own") and src/athena/wiring.py:101-106 ("the gate's character cut is announced only for one episode longer than the cap on its own") both describe behaviour the code cannot reach. Fixed looks like: the first candidate, when alone longer than the room, is packed and left to the READ cap (announced), or the docstrings say it is skipped. This sits next to the recorded agent-memory deviation (packing stops at the first oversized episode, recall.py break) whose fix ad8b82e was reverted whole in fd42e84.

## Flow
- the model calls core.recall for a word found only in one long page dump (a 7,000-char list_claims episode)
- recall_whole -> _whole_episodes: cost > room, items empty, spent = 30 + 42 -> break
- the answer is `(showing 0 of 1)`: the only match is withheld, not cut
- fix order: a test with one oversized match; then either drop the `spent == 0` clause or correct both docstrings; decide together with the reverted packing deviation

## Expected impact
The model gets the head of the only matching page instead of nothing, with the gate's truncation notice. Could break: the paged-reference test copies this branch (tests/core/test_recall.py `_reference_episodes`) and must change with it.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the one oversized match reaches the model, cut and announced
Before: probe, one 7,000-char matching episode, cap 4800: episodes `(showing 0 of 1)`
After: not taken - the change is coupled to the reverted agent-memory packing pair
Method: probe - Before measured on the real tree; After not built because the packing rule is the recorded deviation whose last fix was reverted as a pair
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/core/recall.py:428  if not items and spent == 0 and cost + overhead > cap:
src/athena/core/recall.py:343  spent = _packed_chars(keyword)  (>= len('### keyword\n(showing 0 of 0)') + 2 = 30)
grep '_whole_episodes(' src -> one caller, recall_whole
probe7: recall_whole(brain, 'Northstar', cap=4800) over one 7,000-char episode -> (showing 0 of 1)
instrument: tests/core/test_recall.py: one 7,000-char episode matching the query, recall_whole cap 4800 -> assert shown 1 of 1 and the executor's answer carries the READ cap's truncation notice; red today (0 of 1)

title: An older build opening a newer index lowers its schema_version stamp
body:
## Summary
`Brain.__init__` writes `schema_version = SCHEMA_VERSION` on every open, so an older build that opens an index a newer build migrated stamps it back down, and the newer build then re-runs a migration it already applied.

## Description
src/athena/core/brain/store.py:189-196 reads the stored version only to decide the v1->v2 re-key, then `INSERT OR REPLACE` stamps the running build's own version whatever was stored. src/athena/core/brain/schema.py:14-18 says the stamp exists "so a later migration can tell an old index from a new one instead of guessing from the presence of a column". With a v3 build that adds a column (ad8b82e did exactly this before it was reverted), the sequence v3 open -> v2 open (stamp 2) -> v3 open runs `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` again, which fails with "duplicate column" and the brain does not open. Fixed looks like a stated version-skew policy (never lower the stamp, or refuse to open a newer index read-write) recorded in an ADR, with a test that stamps a higher version and reopens.

## Flow
- a person runs a newer build once (index migrated, stamped 3)
- they go back to this build: Brain() stamps 2
- the newer build again: _stored_version < 3 -> migration re-runs -> OperationalError
- proposal: decide the skew policy, write the ADR, then a 10-line change and its test

## Expected impact
Moving between builds can no longer leave a brain that will not open. Could break: a policy that refuses newer indexes would stop an older build from opening a brain it can read today.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the stamp tells the truth across builds
Before: probe - stamp set to 3 on a real index, Brain() reopened it, the stamp reads 2
After: not taken - the policy (keep the higher stamp vs refuse) is a decision about what older builds may do to a brain
Method: probe - the lowered stamp measured on a real index; the v3 re-migration failure walked from ad8b82e; not built because the choice is a cross-version contract for stored data
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
evidence:
src/athena/core/brain/store.py:189  if _stored_version(self._con) < 2:
src/athena/core/brain/store.py:191-195  INSERT OR REPLACE INTO companion_meta ... ('schema_version', SCHEMA_VERSION)
git show ad8b82e -- src/athena/core/brain/schema.py  (a version-3 migration that added a column, reverted in fd42e84)

title: A writer's importance above the always floor is a promotion the rebuild undoes
body:
## Summary
`write_fact` and `write_procedural` accept any `importance`; at 4 or more the memory joins the always tier, but only `every_turn` is on disk, so the next rebuild silently drops it back to 3.

## Description
src/athena/core/brain/store.py:404-465 writes `importance` to the index row only (unless `every_turn`), src/athena/core/brain/reconcile.py:195-198 restores DEFAULT_IMPORTANCE or ALWAYS_IMPORTANCE from `every_turn: true`, and src/athena/core/recall.py `_always_block` admits importance >= 4. ADR 0071 made `every_turn` the one product path into the always tier; the `importance` parameter is a second door to the same tier that the disk cannot carry. No production caller passes it (src/athena/wiring.py:139 does not), but many tests/core/test_recall.py fixtures do (`importance=ALWAYS_IMPORTANCE_FLOOR`). Fixed looks like: refuse importance >= ALWAYS_IMPORTANCE without every_turn (a policy-tighten), and move the fixtures to `every_turn=True`.

## Flow
- a script or test writes a fact with importance=5 -> it rides every turn
- `athena brain reconcile` -> the fact is importance 3 -> it leaves the always tier, and the rebuild reports nothing
- fix order: a rebuild-parity test over the always tier; the refusal; the fixture moves

## Expected impact
The always tier is the same before and after a rebuild. Could break: every fixture that reaches the tier through importance, 5 sites in tests/core/test_recall.py alone.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one door to the always tier, and it survives a rebuild
Before: probe - a fact written at importance=5 is in the always block; after reconcile_from_disk it is not (True -> False)
After: not taken - the fixture churn makes this an M
Method: probe - Before measured on a real brain; After not built because the fixture migration is past S
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
src/athena/core/brain/store.py:448-450  if every_turn: ... importance = ALWAYS_IMPORTANCE  (else the caller's importance)
src/athena/core/brain/reconcile.py:195-198  importance = DEFAULT_IMPORTANCE; every_turn -> ALWAYS_IMPORTANCE
grep -c 'importance=ALWAYS_IMPORTANCE_FLOOR' tests/core/test_recall.py -> 5
probe8: always before/after rebuild: True False
instrument: tests/core/test_brain_reconcile.py: write a fact at importance=5 without every_turn, take the always block's ids, copy the tree, rebuild, compare ids; red today (1 -> 0)
